notes:
Rows 21 and 22 are a PAIR and should be read together: the same colour family at the two ends of its range, which is what bounds the dynamic range a detector has to cover.

    row 21  pale pink, e-reader screenshot : paper 0.000, mark 0.125, delta 0.125  MISSED
    row 22  vivid pink, cream paper photo  : paper 0.133, mark 0.525, delta 0.392  found

Pink is not the problem. PALENESS is: the same hue is found at 0.392 and lost at 0.125.

And row 21 breaks saturation as a test outright, not merely at the margin. Row 20's pale callout box -- which is NOT a mark and must be refused -- sits at delta 0.196. Row 21 IS a mark and sits at 0.125. A real mark is LESS saturated than a thing that must be rejected, so the ordering is inverted and no threshold exists. Row 10 showed the window was empty; this shows it was never a window.

Its V drop is NEGATIVE (-0.18): a vivid highlighter under a camera light is BRIGHTER than the paper around it. The fill rule is a one-sided test and handles that fine, but it is worth knowing that 'drop from paper' is not always a drop.
